When a customer abandons checkout, the seats stay temporarily blocked as a "hold" for up to 10 minutes; the tide-worker scans holds every 30 seconds and once a hold lapses unpaid, the seats are released back to inventory and the event page cache is invalidated (any late Paylane confirmation on a lapsed hold triggers an automatic refund).

Seats are held temporarily during checkout; if the purchase isn't completed the hold expires after 10 minutes (checked by a worker every 30 seconds), releasing the seats back to inventory and invalidating the event page cache — and any late payment confirmation on an already-lapsed hold triggers an automatic refund.

High-demand drops route buyers into a virtual waiting room (queue page served from Nimbus CDN), admitting them in batches via a token bucket (500/min, signed 15-minute passes), with the worker pool scaled up ahead of time — this eliminated timeouts on a 12,000-buyer drop.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-04-waiting-room.md, tidewater/memory/decisions.md

Each QR token is consumed atomically via a conditional update (`UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`), so only the first scan succeeds and any later attempt at any gate is rejected with "already used" plus the time/gate of the original scan — this fixed BUG-017's race between two gates scanning within seconds of each other.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md (ADR-011), tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md, tidewater/docs/bugs.md

Tickets can't be double-scanned because Gatekeeper performs an atomic "consume" of each QR entry token in tide-api (each token is single-use); a second scan at any gate is rejected with an "already used" message showing the time and gate of the first entry, and offline-mode scans reconcile afterward with conflicts flagged in the venue report.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md, tidewater/memory/architecture.md

TLS certificates are renewed automatically via certbot (DNS challenge on the domain provider) on a systemd timer running every 12 hours, with a deploy hook that reloads HAProxy with zero downtime and an alert if a cert is within 14 days of expiry; if that automation fails, the manual fallback is `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal` on `kelp-1`, followed by rebuilding the HAProxy cert bundle and a `systemctl reload haproxy`.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md

Certificates are Let's Encrypt (90-day validity, renewed automatically every 60 days via certbot timer); if that automation fails, the manual fallback is to run `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal` on `kelp-1`, verify expiry with `openssl x509 -enddate`, rebuild the HAProxy bundle (`haproxy-cert-bundle tidewater.example`), and `systemctl reload haproxy`, then confirm externally with `curl -vI https://tidewater.example`.

Sources: tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md
